Jews were persecuted above all. The wrong options name freedoms that the state did not allow: {{Meinungsfreiheit}}, {{Religionsfreiheit}} and {{Demokratie}}.
rassismus.meaning: racism carried out by the state
rassismus.front: What is it called when the state itself treats people as unequal because of race?

items.q: In which years did the National Socialists rule, and what is the anchor?
Which office did Hitler get in 1933?
items.a: He became {{Reichskanzler}}, the head of the government.

items.q: Which freedoms were missing in the dictatorship?
items.a: {{freie Wahlen}} and {{Pressefreiheit}}. Parties were banned.

items.q: What does {{staatlicher Rassismus}} mean for the Nazi state?
items.a: The state itself treated people as unequal because of a supposed race. It persecuted Jews.

verfolgung-krieg.title: Persecution and war
verfolgung-krieg.big: In 1938 Jewish shops and synagogues were destroyed, and the Second World War of 1939 to 1945 ended with Germany's unconditional surrender.

pogrom.body: On 9 November 1938 National Socialists and their followers destroyed Jewish shops ({{jüdische Geschäfte}}) and synagogues ({{Synagogen}}) in Germany. A {{Synagoge}} is a Jewish house of worship. A {{Pogrom}} is violence against a group of people, here against Jews. It happened five years after Hitler became {{Reichskanzler}}. It was state racism in action.
pogrom.meaning: the night of anti-Jewish violence in 1938
pogrom.front: What was destroyed on 9 November 1938, and by whom?
pogrom.back: Synagogues and Jewish shops, by National Socialists and their followers

falle-polen.text: A wrong option names the attack on Poland. That is a real event, but it happened in 1939 and began the Second World War. It is not the event of 9 November 1938.

weltkrieg.q: Which war began in 1939 and ended in 1945?
weltkrieg.body: The Second World War ({{Zweiter Weltkrieg}}) began in 1939, when German troops attacked Poland. It ended in 1945. The wrong options are other wars. The {{Erste Weltkrieg}} (First World War) came before it. The {{Vietnamkrieg}} and the {{Golfkrieg}} (Gulf War) came after it.
weltkrieg.front: Which war began with the German attack on Poland?

stauffenberg.q: What is Claus Schenk Graf von Stauffenberg known for?
stauffenberg.body: Claus Schenk Graf von Stauffenberg was an officer who joined the resistance ({{Widerstand}}) against Hitler. On 20 July 1944 he made an {{Attentat}} (assassination attempt) on Hitler. A bomb exploded, but Hitler survived. So the attempt failed. The wrong options name a gold medal, the Reichstag building and the build-up of the {{Wehrmacht}} (the army of that time).
stauffenberg.front: What did Claus Schenk Graf von Stauffenberg try on 20 July 1944?

kriegsende.q: When did the Second World War end?
kriegsende.body: The Second World War in Europe ended on 8 May 1945. So the year of the end is 1945, 12 years after 1933. The dictatorship of the National Socialists ended with the war. Other options name later events: Adenauer became Federal Chancellor in 1949, and the Berlin Wall was built in 1961. The year 1933 in the options is the start of the dictatorship.
kriegsende.front: On which date did the war in Europe end?

kapitulation.q: How did the war in Europe officially end?
kapitulation.body: The war ended with the {{bedingungslose Kapitulation}} (unconditional surrender) of Germany. {{Kapitulation}} means surrender. {{Bedingung}} means condition, so {{bedingungslos}} means without any condition. Germany lost the war and could not set any terms.
kapitulation.front: What did Germany have to do to end the war in Europe officially?
kapitulation.back: with the unconditional surrender of Germany
kapitulation.note: Bedingung means condition. Bedingungslos: without conditions.

falle-hitler-tod.text: Hitler died before the end, and a wrong option names his death. But the war ended officially **only** with the surrender of Germany. A revolution in Germany or a withdrawal from the occupied territories did not end it.

items.q: What happened on 9 November 1938?
items.a: National Socialists and their followers destroyed {{Synagogen}} and Jewish shops.

items.q: In which years did Hitler become {{Reichskanzler}}, the Second World War begin and the war end?
What did Stauffenberg do on 20 July 1944, and what was the result?
items.a: He tried to kill Hitler with a bomb. The attempt failed.

items.q: How and when did the war in Europe officially end?
items.a: On 8 May 1945 with the {{bedingungslose Kapitulation}} of Germany. The death of Hitler did not end it.

erinnerung.title: Remembrance and responsibility today
erinnerung.big: Germany remembers the victims of National Socialism, punishes Holocaust denial and feels a special responsibility for Israel.

stolpersteine.body: A {{Stolperstein}} is a small brass plate set into the pavement. {{Stolpern}} means to stumble, {{Stein}} means stone. The plate carries the name of a victim of National Socialism. It lies in front of the house where this person lived. The stones remember people of many groups, not only famous people and not only Jews.
stolpersteine.front: Whom do the small brass plates in German pavements remember?

gedenktag.q: What does the day of remembrance on 27 January commemorate?
gedenktag.body: 27 January is an official {{Gedenktag}} (day of remembrance) in Germany. It remembers the victims of National Socialism. On 27 January 1945 the Auschwitz extermination camp ({{Vernichtungslager}}) was liberated. {{Vernichtung}} means destruction. In a camp like this the National Socialists murdered people.
gedenktag.front: Which victims does Germany remember on 27 January, and why on that day?
gedenktag.back: the victims of National Socialism (liberation of Auschwitz)
gedenktag.note: Not the end of the war. That is 8 May.

falle-gedenktag.text: A wrong option says the end of the Second World War. That was 8 May 1945, not 27 January. The other wrong options, the Basic Law (1949) and reunification (1990), are much later.

holocaust.q: How is the denial of the Holocaust punished?
holocaust.body: The {{Holocaust}} was the murder of about 6 million Jews by the National Socialists. To deny it ({{leugnen}}) is a crime in Germany. The punishment is {{Freiheitsstrafe}} (prison) of up to 5 years or a {{Geldstrafe}} (fine). Community service and cuts in social benefits are not the punishment. Denial is **not** allowed.
holocaust.front: What can happen to a person who denies the murder of the Jews by the National Socialists?
holocaust.back: prison of up to 5 years or a fine

antisemitismus.q: What is an example of antisemitic behaviour?
antisemitismus.body: {{Antisemitismus}} means hostility towards Jews. Denying the Holocaust is an example of antisemitic behaviour. It is also a crime, as the last unit showed. The wrong options are not examples: attending a Jewish festival, criticising the Israeli government, playing football against Jews.
antisemitismus.front: Which behaviour towards the past is antisemitic and also a crime?

israel-aufruf.q: Which acts relating to the State of Israel are prohibited?
israel-aufruf.body: In Germany the public call for the destruction of Israel is prohibited ({{verboten}}). A state may be criticised, and its policy may be discussed. The call to destroy it is something else.
israel-aufruf.meaning: the call for the destruction of Israel
israel-aufruf.front: What public demand about Israel is prohibited?
israel-aufruf.back: the public call for the destruction of Israel

falle-kritik.text: Criticism is not the same as a call for destruction. A wrong option names criticism of Israel's policy, a discussion or an Israeli flag on private property: all three are allowed. Only the public **call** for destruction is prohibited.

verantwortung.q: Where does Germany's special responsibility for Israel come from?
verantwortung.body: Germany has a special responsibility ({{besondere Verantwortung}}) for Israel. It comes from the {{nationalsozialistische Verbrechen}} (National Socialist crimes) against Jews, above all the Holocaust. The wrong options name other things: membership of the EU, the {{Grundgesetz}} (Basic Law) or the Christian tradition.
verantwortung.front: Which part of German history created the special responsibility for Israel?
verantwortung.back: the National Socialist crimes against Jews
verantwortung.note: Not the EU, not the Basic Law.

israel-gruendung.q: On what legal basis was the State of Israel founded?
israel-gruendung.body: In 1947 the {{Vereinten Nationen}} (United Nations) adopted a resolution. On this basis the State of Israel was founded in 1948. The Federal Republic did not exist yet in 1948: it was founded in 1949. So a proposal of the federal government cannot be the basis. A decision of the Zionist Congress or a proposal of the USSR is not the basis either.
israel-gruendung.front: Which international organisation made the decision on which Israel was founded?
israel-gruendung.back: a resolution of the United Nations
israel-gruendung.note: Founded 1948, three years after the end of the war.

items.q: Whom do the {{Stolpersteine}} and the day of remembrance on 27 January remember?
items.a: The victims of National Socialism. On 27 January 1945 Auschwitz was liberated.

items.q: What happens in Germany to a person who denies the Holocaust?
items.a: It is antisemitic and a crime: prison of up to 5 years, or a fine.

items.q: Which statement about Israel is prohibited in Germany, and which is allowed?
items.a: The public call for the destruction of Israel is prohibited. Criticising Israel's policy is allowed.

items.q: Why does Germany have a special responsibility for Israel?
items.a: Because of the National Socialist crimes against Jews.

besatzung.title: Occupation and the four zones
besatzung.big: After 1945 four Allied powers ruled Germany in four zones, and the GDR was later founded in the Soviet zone.

besatzungsmaechte.q: Which four countries ruled Germany after 1945?
besatzungsmaechte.body: After the war four countries ruled Germany: the USA, the Soviet Union, Great Britain and France. They are the {{Alliierte Besatzungsmächte}} (Allied occupying powers). {{Alliierte}} means allies: they had fought together against Nazi Germany. Japan was **not** one of them. Poland, Sweden, Italy, Spain and Portugal were not occupying powers either.
besatzungsmaechte.front: Which four countries ruled Germany after the war?
besatzungsmaechte.back: USA, Soviet Union, Great Britain, France
besatzungsmaechte.note: Japan was never an occupying power in Germany.

zonen.q: How many zones were there, and which power ruled which?
zonen.body: After 1945 Germany was divided into 4 {{Besatzungszonen}} (occupation zones). Each of the four powers ruled one zone. Great Britain ruled the north-west, the Soviet Union the east, the USA the south and France the south-west.
zonen.front: Which power ruled the north-west, the east, the south and the south-west?
zonen.back: Great Britain, Soviet Union, USA, France (4 zones)
zonen.note: East is Soviet. The French zone lies at the French border.

zonen-bild.caption: In this picture zone 1 (north-west) is the British zone and zone 2 (east) is the Soviet zone. Zone 3 (south) is the American zone and zone 4 (south-west) is the French zone. The small area inside zone 2 is Berlin.

sowjetzone.q: In which zone was the GDR founded?
sowjetzone.body: The GDR was founded in 1949 in the Soviet zone ({{sowjetische Besatzungszone}}). The Soviet zone was the east of Germany. The Federal Republic was founded in the three western zones: the American, the British and the French zone.
sowjetzone.front: Which power ruled the zone in which the GDR began?
sowjetzone.note: The GDR began in the east, in the Soviet zone.

berlin.q: Which German city was divided into four sectors?
berlin.body: Berlin was divided into four {{Sektoren}} (sectors), one for each power. A zone is a part of a country. A sector is a part of a city. Berlin lay inside the Soviet zone, but all four powers shared the city. Munich, Dresden and Frankfurt (Oder) were not divided into sectors.
berlin.meaning: the sector, a part of a city
berlin.front: Which city did the four powers share after 1945?
berlin.note: A zone is a part of a country, a sector of a city.

karte-zonen.caption: Find Berlin inside the Soviet zone. All four powers shared the city.

luftbruecke.q: Why was West Berlin supplied by aircraft in 1948 and 1949?
luftbruecke.body: The three western sectors formed West Berlin. It lay inside the Soviet zone, like an island, so every road and railway to it crossed the Soviet zone. From June 1948 to May 1949 the Soviet Union cut off all traffic by land. The western powers then supplied the city by aircraft. This is the {{Luftbrücke}}: {{Luft}} means air, {{Brücke}} means bridge.
luftbruecke.case: In 1948 the people of West Berlin got food and coal from aircraft, not from trucks or trains.
luftbruecke.front: What made aircraft the only way to supply West Berlin in 1948?
luftbruecke.back: The Soviet Union cut off all traffic by land.
luftbruecke.note: West Berlin: an island inside the Soviet zone.

falle-luftbruecke.text: Wrong options say that the airlift was cheaper, faster or safer for the western powers. That is not the reason. The reason was that the Soviet Union cut off all traffic by land.

items.q: Which four countries were the Allied occupying powers, and which country was not one?
items.a: The USA, the Soviet Union, Great Britain and France. Japan was not one.

items.q: Which zone later became the GDR, and which zones became the Federal Republic?
items.a: The Soviet zone became the GDR. The three western zones became the Federal Republic.

items.q: Why did aircraft supply West Berlin in 1948 and 1949?
items.a: West Berlin lay inside the Soviet zone like an island. The Soviet Union cut off all traffic by land.

items.q: What is the difference between a {{Zone}} and a {{Sektor}}?
items.a: A {{Zone}} is a part of a country. A {{Sektor}} is a part of a city, here Berlin.

zwei-staaten.title: Two German states from 1949
zwei-staaten.big: In 1949 two German states were founded: the Federal Republic in the west and the GDR in the east.

brd-gruendung.q: When was the Federal Republic founded?
brd-gruendung.body: The Federal Republic of Germany was founded in 1949, in the three western zones. The Second World War began in 1939 and ended in 1945. The new state came four years after the end of the war. In the same year the GDR was founded in the east.
brd-gruendung.front: In which year did the Federal Republic begin, four years after the war ended?
brd-gruendung.note: The GDR was founded in the same year.

adenauer.q: Who was the first Federal Chancellor?
adenauer.body: Konrad Adenauer was the first {{Bundeskanzler}} (Federal Chancellor) of the Federal Republic. He took office in 1949 and was chancellor until 1963. Brandt, Schmidt, Kiesinger, Erhard and Schröder were all chancellors after him.
adenauer.front: Who led the government as chancellor from 1949?
adenauer.note: The first chancellor. The other names came later.

wirtschaftswunder.q: When was the economic miracle in the Federal Republic?
wirtschaftswunder.body: The {{Wirtschaftswunder}} (economic miracle) was a time of very fast growth of the economy in the Federal Republic. It was in the 1950s. {{Wirtschaft}} means economy and {{Wunder}} means miracle. In most of the 1940s there was war or occupation, not growth.
wirtschaftswunder.front: Which decade was the time of very fast economic growth in the Federal Republic?
wirtschaftswunder.note: Adenauer was chancellor in those years.

ddr-name.q: What does the abbreviation DDR stand for?
ddr-name.body: {{DDR}} stands for {{Deutsche Demokratische Republik}}. In English this is the German Democratic Republic (GDR). It was the German state in the east. {{Deutsche}} means German, {{Demokratische}} means democratic and {{Republik}} means republic.
ddr-name.front: Which three German words are behind the letters DDR?
ddr-name.note: There is no word for third in the name.

falle-ddr.text: The wrong options contain {{Dritter}} or {{Dritte}} (third) or leave out the word {{Demokratische}}. The three letters D, D, R are {{Deutsche}}, {{Demokratische}}, {{Republik}}. {{Rundfunk}} means radio, so that option is not a state.

ddr-zeit.q: When was the GDR founded, and how long did it exist?
ddr-zeit.body: The GDR was founded in 1949 in the Soviet zone. It existed until 1990. That is about 40 years. The years 1933 to 1945 are the Nazi dictatorship, not the GDR.
ddr-zeit.front: From which year to which year did the GDR exist?
ddr-zeit.note: 1949 plus 40 years is 1989. It ended in 1990.

kniefall.q: What did Willy Brandt express by kneeling in Warsaw in 1970?
kniefall.body: In 1970 Federal Chancellor Willy Brandt knelt down at the memorial in the former Jewish ghetto in Warsaw. This {{Kniefall}} (kneeling) was a request for forgiveness. Brandt asked Poland and the Polish Jews for forgiveness. The reason was the crimes that Germans committed in Poland under the National Socialists.
kniefall.front: What did the silent kneeling of a German chancellor in Warsaw mean?
kniefall.back: He asked Poland and the Polish Jews for forgiveness.

kniefall-bild.caption: Willy Brandt kneels in Warsaw in 1970. People stand behind him. The kneeling is a sign of asking for forgiveness, not of submission.

falle-kniefall.text: Wrong options say that Brandt submitted to the former Allies or prayed at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. He did neither, and he did not show humility before the {{Warschauer Pakt}} (Warsaw Pact), the alliance of the East. He asked for forgiveness.

ostvertraege.q: Which politician stands for the Eastern Treaties?
ostvertraege.body: Willy Brandt stands for the {{Ostverträge}} (Eastern Treaties). {{Ost}} means east and {{Verträge}} means treaties. They were agreements with states of the East, such as Poland and the Soviet Union. They improved relations with the East. Michail Gorbatschow (Mikhail Gorbachev) led the Soviet Union and was not a German chancellor.
ostvertraege.front: Which German politician is linked with treaties with the East in the 1970s?
ostvertraege.note: Brandt: kneeling in Warsaw and the Ostverträge.

items.q: Why is 1945 wrong as the founding year of the two German states?
items.a: In 1945 the war ended and the occupation began. Both states followed in 1949.

items.q: Who was the first Federal Chancellor, and in which decade was the {{Wirtschaftswunder}}?
items.a: Konrad Adenauer. The {{Wirtschaftswunder}} was in the 1950s.

items.q: What do the letters DDR stand for, and in which years did the GDR exist?
items.a: {{Deutsche Demokratische Republik}}. It existed from 1949 to 1990.

items.q: What did Willy Brandt ask for in Warsaw, and which treaties stand for him?
items.a: He asked Poland and the Polish Jews for forgiveness. The {{Ostverträge}} (Eastern Treaties) stand for him.

ddr.title: Life in the GDR and the Cold War
ddr.big: The GDR belonged to the Warsaw Pact, had a planned economy and was a dictatorship with a secret service, the Stasi.

eiserner-vorhang.body: The expression {{Eiserner Vorhang}} (Iron Curtain) names the closed border between East and West in Europe. {{Eisern}} means made of iron and {{Vorhang}} means curtain. It stands for the sealing off of the {{Warschauer Pakt}} (Warsaw Pact) against the West. It has nothing to do with north and south Germany.
eiserner-vorhang.front: Who sealed itself off from the West behind the Iron Curtain?
eiserner-vorhang.note: A curtain between East and West, not north and south.

warschauer-pakt.q: Which military alliance did the GDR belong to?
warschauer-pakt.body: After 1945 the {{Kalter Krieg}} (Cold War) was a long conflict between the West and the East. The GDR belonged to the East. It was a member of the {{Warschauer Pakt}} (Warsaw Pact), a military alliance. The Federal Republic belonged to the West, to the {{NATO}}.
warschauer-pakt.front: In the Cold War the GDR was on the side of the East. In which alliance?
warschauer-pakt.note: The Federal Republic was in NATO.

falle-bund.text: The GDR was never in the {{NATO}} and did not belong to the {{Westmächte}} (Western powers). It was also not a {{blockfreier Staat}} (a state in neither alliance). {{Rheinbund}} and {{Europabündnis}} are not the answer either.

planwirtschaft.q: Which economic system did the GDR have?
planwirtschaft.body: The economy of the GDR was a {{Planwirtschaft}} (planned economy). {{Plan}} means plan and {{Wirtschaft}} means economy. The state planned what was produced and what things cost. The Federal Republic had a {{Marktwirtschaft}} (market economy), where supply and demand set the prices. The other options describe a market economy, the opposite of a plan.
planwirtschaft.front: In the GDR the state planned production and prices. What was this system called?
planwirtschaft.note: Plan: the state decides. Market: supply and demand decide.

stasi.body: {{Stasi}} is the short form of {{Staatssicherheit}} (state security). The full name was {{Ministerium für Staatssicherheit}}, the Ministry for State Security. It was the secret service ({{Geheimdienst}}) of the GDR. It watched the people of the GDR, which was a {{Diktatur}} (dictatorship). It was not the secret service of the {{Drittes Reich}} (Third Reich).
stasi.meaning: the secret service of the GDR
stasi.front: Which authority of the GDR was its secret service?
stasi.back: the Stasi, the Ministry for State Security

volksaufstand.q: What happened in the GDR on 17 June 1953?
volksaufstand.body: On 17 June 1953 there were strikes all over the GDR and a {{Volksaufstand}} (popular uprising). {{Volk}} means people and {{Aufstand}} means uprising. The uprising was put down by force. For a long time 17 June was a public holiday in the Federal Republic, to remember the uprising.
volksaufstand.front: In 1953 there were strikes and an uprising in the GDR. Which day is remembered?
volksaufstand.back: 17 June: nationwide strikes and a popular uprising
volksaufstand.note: In the West, a public holiday remembered it.

falle-daten.text: 1 May is Labour Day, not the uprising. 20 July 1944 is the attempt on Hitler. 9 November 1989 is the day the Wall was opened.

ddr-wappen.q: How do you recognise the flag and coat of arms of the GDR?
ddr-wappen.body: The GDR flag had the same three colours as the flag of today: {{schwarz-rot-gold}}. In the middle it showed the coat of arms ({{Wappen}}) of the GDR. The coat of arms is {{Hammer, Zirkel und Ährenkranz}}: a hammer, a compass and a wreath of ears of grain. The flag of the Federal Republic has no such sign, and its coat of arms shows an eagle.
ddr-wappen.meaning: the coat of arms of the GDR
ddr-wappen.front: Which sign is in the middle of the GDR flag and coat of arms?
ddr-wappen.back: hammer, compass and wreath of ears of grain
ddr-wappen.note: Same colours as today's flag, plus this sign.

flagge-bild.caption: The flag of the GDR: black, red, gold with hammer, compass and a wreath of ears of grain in the middle. The flag of the Federal Republic has no sign.

wappen-bild.caption: Picture 4 is the coat of arms of the GDR: hammer and compass inside a wreath of ears of grain. Picture 1 is the eagle of the Federal Republic. Pictures 2 and 3 are not state coats of arms.

items.q: Which military alliance did the GDR belong to, and which one the Federal Republic?
items.a: The GDR to the {{Warschauer Pakt}}. The Federal Republic to the {{NATO}}.

items.q: What is the difference between a {{Planwirtschaft}} and a {{Marktwirtschaft}}?
items.a: In a {{Planwirtschaft}} the state plans production and prices. In a {{Marktwirtschaft}} supply and demand decide.

items.q: What was the {{Stasi}}, and what is its full name?
items.a: The secret service of the GDR. Its full name was {{Ministerium für Staatssicherheit}}.

items.q: What happened on 17 June 1953, and how did the Federal Republic remember it?
items.a: Strikes and a popular uprising in the GDR. In the Federal Republic 17 June was a public holiday for a long time.

mauer-wende.title: The Wall and the turning point
mauer-wende.big: From 1961 to 1989 a wall divided Berlin; in 1989 peaceful protests brought the change to democracy, and the Wall was opened.

mauerbau.q: Who built the Wall in Berlin, and when?
mauerbau.body: The GDR built the Wall ({{Mauer}}) in Berlin in 1961. The Federal Republic and the Western powers did not build it. The Wall stood for 28 years, until 1989.
mauerbau.front: Which state built the Berlin Wall, and in which year?

berlin-geteilt.q: What was Berlin like from 1961 to 1989?
berlin-geteilt.body: From 1961 to 1989 Berlin was divided by a wall. The Wall split the city into East Berlin and West Berlin. Do not mix it up with 1948 and 1949: then aircraft supplied West Berlin, but there was no wall.
berlin-geteilt.front: In which years did a wall divide the city of Berlin?
berlin-geteilt.note: Wall, not airlift: the airlift was in 1948 and 1949.

montagsdemos.q: Which protests in 1989 shouted {{Wir sind das Volk}}?
montagsdemos.body: In autumn 1989 many people in the GDR went to demonstrations on Mondays. These are the {{Montagsdemonstrationen}} (Monday demonstrations). They shouted {{Wir sind das Volk}}, which means: we are the people. The demonstrations were peaceful.
montagsdemos.front: In 1989 people in the GDR shouted that they were the people. At which protests?
montagsdemos.back: at the Monday demonstrations of 1989 in the GDR

falle-1953.text: The workers' uprising of 1953 was also in the GDR, but the call {{Wir sind das Volk}} belongs to 1989. The protests of 1968 and 1985 took place in the Federal Republic.

wende.q: What changed in the GDR in autumn 1989?
wende.body: {{Wende}} means turning point. In autumn 1989 the GDR changed politically from a {{Diktatur}} (dictatorship) to a {{Demokratie}} (democracy). The GDR was never a monarchy or a religious state. Its economy was planned, not a liberal market economy.
wende.front: In autumn 1989 the GDR changed politically. From what to what?
wende.back: from a dictatorship to a democracy

mauerfall.q: When was the Wall opened for everyone?
mauerfall.body: The Wall in Berlin was opened for everyone in 1989. The day was 9 November 1989. After 28 years of division, people could cross between East and West Berlin. The Wall opened in the year before German unity (1990), so 1992 and 1995 are too late.
mauerfall.front: One year before German unity the Berlin Wall opened. Which year?

items.q: Who built the Wall in Berlin, and in which year?
items.a: The GDR built it in 1961.

items.q: For how many years did the Wall divide Berlin?
items.a: From 1961 to 1989: 28 years.

items.q: What did people shout at the Monday demonstrations of 1989?
items.a: {{Wir sind das Volk}}: we are the people.

items.q: What changed politically in the GDR in the autumn of 1989?
items.a: The GDR changed from a dictatorship to a democracy. This is called {{Die Wende}}.

einheit.title: German unity in 1990
einheit.big: On 3 October 1990 the five eastern states joined the Federal Republic, and Germany was one state again.

einheitstag.q: What does Germany celebrate on 3 October?
einheitstag.body: On 3 October Germany celebrates the {{Tag der Deutschen Einheit}} (Day of German Unity). It remembers 3 October 1990, when the GDR joined the Federal Republic. {{Einheit}} means unity. It is a public holiday in the whole country.
einheitstag.front: What is the name of the holiday on 3 October?
einheitstag.note: 3 October 1990: the GDR joined the Federal Republic.

beitritt.q: How did the two German states become one state?
beitritt.body: On 3 October 1990 the five eastern states joined the Federal Republic. In German this is a {{Beitritt}} (accession). It is generally called {{Deutsche Wiedervereinigung}} (German reunification). The Federal Republic stayed the same state, with the same name and the same Basic Law ({{Grundgesetz}}). So the new states now belong to the European Union too, because the Federal Republic was already a member.
beitritt.front: How did the GDR and the Federal Republic become one state, and what is it called?
beitritt.back: Accession of the eastern states: German reunification
beitritt.note: The East joined the West. Nobody occupied anyone.

falle-richtung.text: Wrong options say that one state occupied the other, or that the western states joined the GDR. Both are wrong. The East joined the Federal Republic, and nobody was occupied.

falle-erweiterung.text: {{Osterweiterung}} means enlargement to the east. {{NATO-Osterweiterung}} and {{EU-Osterweiterung}} name the later entry of eastern European states, not German unity. The {{Europäische Gemeinschaft}} was the forerunner of the EU.

fuenf-laender.q: Which five states joined the Federal Republic in 1990?
fuenf-laender.body: In 1990 five states joined the Federal Republic: {{Brandenburg}}, {{Mecklenburg-Vorpommern}}, {{Sachsen}}, {{Sachsen-Anhalt}} and {{Thüringen}}. In English: Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia. These five states were the territory of the GDR, in the east of Germany. Do not mix up {{Sachsen}} with {{Niedersachsen}} (Lower Saxony): Lower Saxony lies in the west. The other options are states of the west or the south, such as {{Bayern}} (Bavaria), {{Hessen}} (Hesse) and {{Saarland}}.
fuenf-laender.meaning: the new federal states in the east
fuenf-laender.front: Which five of today's federal states were in the GDR?
fuenf-laender.back: Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia
fuenf-laender.note: All five lie in the east. Lower Saxony is not one.

karte-osten.caption: The five marked states were the territory of the GDR. East Berlin, its capital, joined West Berlin and became part of the one state of Berlin.

grenzen.q: Since when does Germany have the borders of today?
grenzen.body: The Federal Republic has had the borders of today since 1990. Before that there were two German states with a border between them. With unity the five eastern states joined, and this border ended. 1949 is too early: then the Federal Republic did not yet include the East.
grenzen.front: Since which year has the Federal Republic had the same borders as now?
grenzen.note: The year the East joined the Federal Republic.

kohl.q: Who is called the Chancellor of German Unity?
kohl.body: Helmut Kohl is called the {{Kanzler der Deutschen Einheit}} (Chancellor of German Unity). He was Federal Chancellor when the GDR joined the Federal Republic in 1990. Gerhard Schröder, Konrad Adenauer and Helmut Schmidt were chancellors at other times.
kohl.front: Which chancellor was in office when Germany became one state in 1990?

kanzler.title: Three chancellors, three dates
head: Konrad Adenauer
Willy Brandt
Helmut Kohl
rows: the founding of the Federal Republic
the GDR joins the Federal Republic

items.q: How did the two German states become one state in 1990?
items.a: The five eastern states joined the Federal Republic. This {{Beitritt}} is called {{Deutsche Wiedervereinigung}}.

items.q: Why do the new federal states belong to the European Union?
items.a: They joined the Federal Republic, and the Federal Republic was already a member.

items.q: Name the five states of the former GDR.
items.a: {{Brandenburg}}, {{Mecklenburg-Vorpommern}}, {{Sachsen}}, {{Sachsen-Anhalt}}, {{Thüringen}}.

items.q: Which chancellor stands for 1949, which for 1970 and which for 1990?
items.a: Adenauer for 1949, Brandt for 1970 and Kohl for 1990.

nachbarn.title: Germany's nine neighbours
nachbarn.big: Germany has 9 neighbours, and you can name them all by going round the map clockwise from the north.

nachbarn.body: A {{Nachbarland}} shares a border with Germany. Germany has 9 neighbours. Go round the map clockwise from the north: {{Dänemark}}, {{Polen}}, {{Tschechien}}, {{Österreich}}, {{die Schweiz}}, {{Frankreich}}, {{Luxemburg}}, {{Belgien}}, {{die Niederlande}}. In English: Denmark, Poland, Czechia, Austria, Switzerland, France, Luxembourg, Belgium, the Netherlands.
nachbarn.front: Name the 9 neighbours of Germany, going clockwise from the north.
nachbarn.back: Denmark, Poland, Czechia, Austria, Switzerland, France, Luxembourg, Belgium, the Netherlands
nachbarn.note: Start in the north and go round clockwise.

karte-nachbarn.caption: Germany in the middle with its 9 neighbours. Find each one and say its German name.

falle-fern.text: The wrong options do not touch Germany: {{Ungarn}}, {{Rumänien}}, {{Bulgarien}}, {{Griechenland}} (south-east); {{Spanien}}, {{Portugal}} (south-west); {{Finnland}}, {{Norwegen}}, {{Schweden}} (north). In the north only {{Dänemark}} touches Germany.

oesterreich.q: Which country has a large German-speaking population?
oesterreich.body: German is the official language of {{Österreich}} (Austria). So Austria has a large {{deutschsprachig}} population. The wrong options are {{Tschechien}}, {{Norwegen}} and {{Spanien}}. Czechia borders Germany, but people there speak Czech.
oesterreich.front: Which country has German as its official language: Austria or Czechia?

items.q: How can you hold the 9 neighbours of Germany in your head?
items.a: Go round the map clockwise from the north: {{Dänemark}}, {{Polen}}, {{Tschechien}}, {{Österreich}}, {{die Schweiz}}, {{Frankreich}}, {{Luxemburg}}, {{Belgien}}, {{die Niederlande}}.

items.q: Which country in the north has a border with Germany?
items.a: {{Dänemark}}. {{Schweden}}, {{Norwegen}} and {{Finnland}} do not touch Germany.

items.q: Which has a large {{deutschsprachig}} population: {{Österreich}} or {{Tschechien}}?
items.a: {{Österreich}}. People in Czechia speak Czech.

eu.title: The European Union: name, founding and aims
eu.big: The EU grew out of the Treaties of Rome of 1957, and its states work together for peace and security.

eu-name.q: What does the abbreviation EU stand for?
eu-name.body: {{EU}} is the short form of {{Europäische Union}}. It is a union of European states. The wrong options sound similar: {{Europäische Unternehmen}} (European companies), {{Einheitliche Union}} (uniform union) and {{Euro Union}}. The {{EU}} is named after Europe, not after the euro.
eu-name.front: What do the letters EU stand for?
eu-name.note: E is for Europe, not for euro.

integration.body: {{Europäische Integration}} means that European states join together. The German word for this joining is {{Zusammenschluss}}. The result is the {{EU}}.
integration.front: In one sentence, what is European integration?
integration.back: The union of European states in the EU
integration.note: It is about states, not people.

falle-integration.text: The wrong options talk about immigrants and emigrants, so about people. But {{europäische Integration}} is about **states**.

roemische-vertraege.body: In 1957 the Federal Republic and five other states signed the {{Römische Verträge}} (Treaties of Rome). With them they founded the {{Europäische Wirtschaftsgemeinschaft}} ({{EWG}}), the European Economic Community. {{Wirtschaft}} means economy and {{Gemeinschaft}} means community. Today's {{EU}} grew from this community. The wrong options are the treaties of Hamburg, Paris or London, or topics like NATO, reparations and the eastern border.
roemische-vertraege.front: What did the Treaties of Rome (1957) found?
roemische-vertraege.note: Rome 1957. Not Hamburg, Paris or London.

gruendungsmitglied.q: Of which organisation is Germany a founding member?
gruendungsmitglied.body: The Federal Republic is a founding member of the {{EU}}. It was one of the six states that signed the {{Römische Verträge}} in 1957. The wrong options are other organisations: {{NATO}}, the United Nations and the {{Warschauer Pakt}} (Warsaw Pact). {{NATO}} and the United Nations already existed when the Federal Republic joined them. It was never in the {{Warschauer Pakt}}, the military alliance of the East.
gruendungsmitglied.front: Germany is a founding member of which organisation: EU, NATO or the UN?
gruendungsmitglied.note: It joined NATO and the UN later: both already existed.

mitgliedstaaten.q: How many member states does the EU have?
mitgliedstaaten.body: The {{EU}} has 27 member states ({{Mitgliedstaaten}}) today. {{Mitglied}} means member and {{Staat}} means state. The wrong options are 21, 23 and 25. Remember 27 as the highest of the four numbers.
mitgliedstaaten.front: How many states belong to the EU today?
mitgliedstaaten.note: 27 is the largest of the four options.

eu-flagge.q: What does the flag of the EU look like?
eu-flagge.body: The flag of the {{EU}} is blue with a circle of 12 gold stars. The 12 stars do not count the member states. The wrong pictures show other flags, for example those of the USA and the United Nations.
eu-flagge.front: What does the EU flag look like?
eu-flagge.back: blue with a circle of gold stars
eu-flagge.note: The number of stars is not 27.

bild-flagge.caption: Picture 2 is the flag of the {{EU}}: a circle of gold stars on blue. Picture 1 is the flag of the USA and picture 3 the flag of the United Nations. Picture 4 is another blue flag with a yellow sign.

frieden.q: Which aim of the EU shows in the picture from Verdun?
frieden.body: After two world wars, European states joined together so that war between them does not happen again. So an aim of the {{EU}} is {{Frieden und Sicherheit}} (peace and security) in its countries. The picture shows President François Mitterrand of France and Federal Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Verdun. Together they remember the dead of both world wars.
frieden.front: What is a main aim of the EU?
frieden.back: Peace and security in the countries of the EU
frieden.note: Two leaders remember the dead together.

bild-verdun.caption: The French President and the German Federal Chancellor hold hands in Verdun. In front of them lie a French and a German flag between two wreaths. The picture shows the aim: peace between former enemies.

falle-reisefreiheit.text: Wrong options: {{Reisefreiheit}} (freedom to travel) and friendship between England and Germany. The picture shows a President of France and the Chancellor of Germany, remembering the dead of two wars. That points to **peace**, not to travel.

items.q: Which treaties of 1957 founded the {{EWG}}, and what does {{EWG}} stand for?
items.a: The {{Römische Verträge}}. {{EWG}} is the {{Europäische Wirtschaftsgemeinschaft}}, the European Economic Community. The Federal Republic was one of six founding states.

items.q: Why is {{europäische Integration}} not about immigrants?
items.a: It means the union of European states in the {{EU}}. It is about states, not people.

items.q: How many member states does the {{EU}} have, and what is on its flag?
items.a: 27 member states. The flag is blue with a circle of 12 gold stars.

items.q: Which aim of the {{EU}} do the two leaders in Verdun show?
items.a: {{Frieden und Sicherheit}}: peace and security between the countries of the {{EU}}.

eu-alltag.title: Schengen, the euro and the European Parliament
eu-alltag.big: Schengen means travel without passport control, the euro has been cash since 2002, and voters elect the European Parliament every 5 years.

schengen.q: What does the Schengen Agreement mean for travel?
schengen.body: Germany is a member of the {{Schengener Abkommen}} (Schengen Agreement). So Germans can travel to many countries in Europe without {{Passkontrolle}}. {{Pass}} means passport and {{Kontrolle}} means check. It is about travel, not about money.
schengen.front: What does the Schengen Agreement allow?
schengen.back: Travel to many countries in Europe without passport control
schengen.note: Many European countries, not every country.

falle-schengen.text: Wrong options say Germans can travel to **any** country, or that all people can enter Germany freely. Schengen only means travel without passport control in many countries in Europe. Paying with the euro in any country is a different topic.

euro-bargeld.q: Since when do people in Germany pay cash with the euro?
euro-bargeld.body: Since 2002 people in Germany pay cash with the euro, with euro notes and coins. {{Bar}} means cash and {{Geld}} means money. The wrong years are 1995, 1998 and 2005. Not every country uses the euro.
euro-bargeld.front: Since which year are euro notes and coins the cash in Germany?

europawahl-takt.q: How often is the European Parliament elected?
europawahl-takt.body: The {{Europawahl}} takes place every 5 years. {{Europa}} means Europe and {{Wahl}} means election. The wrong answers are 6, 7 and 8 years.
europawahl-takt.front: How many years are there between two European elections?

europawahl-wen.q: Who is elected in the European election?
europawahl-wen.body: In the {{Europawahl}} people elect the {{Abgeordneten}} (members) of the {{Europäisches Parlament}}. They do **not** choose the {{Europäische Kommission}} (European Commission), new member countries or a European constitution. The verb is {{wählen}}: to elect.
europawahl-wen.front: Whom do people elect in the European election?
europawahl-wen.back: the members of the European Parliament

wahlkette.caption: Voters elect the members, and the members together form the Parliament.

parlament-orte.q: Where does the European Parliament work?
parlament-orte.body: The {{Europäisches Parlament}} works in three places: {{Straßburg}} (Strasbourg), {{Luxemburg}} (Luxembourg) and {{Brüssel}} (Brussels). Strasbourg is a seat ({{Sitz}}) of the Parliament. The three cities lie in France, Luxembourg and Belgium, all neighbours of Germany. The wrong options name other cities, for example Paris, London or Rome.
parlament-orte.front: Name the three places where the European Parliament works.
parlament-orte.note: All three lie in neighbours of Germany.

karte-parlament.caption: Find Strasbourg, Luxembourg and Brussels on the map. All three lie in neighbours of Germany.

items.q: What does the Schengen Agreement mean for Germans?
items.a: They can travel to many countries in Europe without {{Passkontrolle}}. It is not about paying with the euro.

items.q: Since when is the euro cash in Germany?
items.a: Since 2002. Not every country uses the euro.

items.q: Who is elected in the {{Europawahl}}, and how often?
items.a: The {{Abgeordneten}} of the {{Europäisches Parlament}}, every 5 years. The {{Europäische Kommission}} is not elected in it.

items.q: Where does the {{Europäisches Parlament}} work, and in which countries are these places?
items.a: {{Straßburg}}, {{Luxemburg}} and {{Brüssel}}: in France, Luxembourg and Belgium, all neighbours of Germany.

gerichte.title: Courts and the people in them
gerichte.big: Judges and lay judges decide in court, lawyers advise and represent people, and the police make sure that laws are obeyed.

prozess.q: What is a trial, and when does one take place?
prozess.body: A procedure before a court is called a {{Prozess}} (a trial). A criminal trial takes place when someone has committed a crime ({{Straftat}}) and is charged ({{angeklagt}}). Changing religion, holding another opinion or parking wrongly is not a crime. The words {{Programm}}, {{Prozedur}} and {{Protokoll}} also begin with Pro-, but they are wrong.
prozess.front: What is a court procedure called, and when does one take place?
prozess.back: the trial, when someone has committed a crime and is charged
prozess.note: A crime plus a charge leads to a trial.

richter.body: A judge ({{Richterin}} or {{Richter}}) works at a court and passes judgments ({{Urteile}}). The German phrase for this work is {{Recht sprechen}}, to administer justice: to decide a case by the law. A judge does not govern, does not draw up plans and does not enact laws. Representing people in court is the work of a lawyer.
richter.front: What is the main task of a judge?
richter.back: works at a court and passes judgments (administers justice)
richter.note: A judge decides. A lawyer represents.

gewalt.q: Which branch of state power does a judge belong to?
gewalt.body: State power in Germany is divided into three parts. A judge belongs to the judiciary, in German the {{Judikative}}. Two other German words name the same power: {{rechtsprechende Gewalt}} (the judging power) and {{Rechtsprechung}}. All three words mean the power that judges by the law.
gewalt.front: Which state power do judges belong to? Give the German words.
gewalt.back: the judiciary, the judging power, the administration of justice
gewalt.note: Not Exekutive (carries out) and not Legislative (makes laws).

gewalten.title: The three powers
head: {{Legislative}}
{{Exekutive}}
{{Judikative}}
rows: decides court cases by the laws

falle-gewalt.text: Wrong options are {{Operative}}, {{planende Gewalt}} (planning power) and {{Presse}}. None of them is a state power. The three state powers are {{Legislative}}, {{Exekutive}} and {{Judikative}}.

schoeffe.q: What is a lay judge, and what does he or she do?
schoeffe.body: A lay judge ({{Schöffin}} or {{Schöffe}}) is an honorary judge: an {{ehrenamtliche Richterin}} or {{ehrenamtlicher Richter}}. An {{Ehrenamt}} is an honorary office, a task for citizens and not a career. A lay judge does not need to have studied law. In a trial, lay judges decide together with the judges on guilt ({{Schuld}}) and punishment ({{Strafe}}).
schoeffe.front: What kind of judge is a lay judge, and what does he or she decide?
schoeffe.back: an honorary judge who decides on guilt and punishment together with the judges
schoeffe.note: Not a lawyer: no advice, no defence.

anwalt.q: Who advises people on legal questions and represents them in court?
anwalt.body: A lawyer ({{Rechtsanwältin}} or {{Rechtsanwalt}}) advises people on legal questions ({{Rechtsfragen}}). A lawyer also represents them in court. {{Recht}} means law, and an {{Anwalt}} is someone who acts for another person. A public prosecutor ({{Staatsanwalt}}) has another task: he or she brings the charge for the state.
anwalt.front: Which person helps you with legal problems and speaks for you at court?
anwalt.note: Not the judge, not the lay judge.

gericht-rollen.title: Who does what in court?
head: {{Richter}}
{{Schöffe}}
{{Rechtsanwalt}}
rows: decides on guilt and punishment with the judges

falle-schoeffe.text: Wrong options for the lay judge describe a lawyer: gives legal advice and defends the accused ({{Angeklagte}}). A lay judge takes no side. He or she decides together with the judges.

polizei.q: What is a task of the police?
polizei.body: The police make sure that laws are obeyed: they monitor compliance with the laws ({{die Einhaltung von Gesetzen überwachen}}). They belong to the {{Exekutive}}, the power that carries out the laws. Other tasks belong to other bodies: a parliament passes the laws, and the armed forces ({{Bundeswehr}}) defend the country.
polizei.front: What do the police do in Germany?
polizei.back: monitor that the laws are obeyed
polizei.note: Police watch laws, parliament passes them, army defends.

items.q: What is a court procedure called, and when does one take place?
items.a: A {{Prozess}}. It takes place when someone has committed a crime ({{Straftat}}) and is charged.

items.q: Which state power do judges belong to, and what are its two German names?
items.a: {{Judikative}} or {{rechtsprechende Gewalt}}. Their work is {{Recht sprechen}}.

items.q: What is the difference between a lay judge and a lawyer?
items.a: A lay judge is an honorary judge and decides with the judges on guilt and punishment. A lawyer advises and represents people.

items.q: How do the powers of the police and of the judges differ?
items.a: The police watch that laws are obeyed ({{Exekutive}}). Judges pass judgments ({{Judikative}}).

familienrecht.title: Rules for personal life
familienrecht.big: German law fixes ages (18 and 14), protects children, allows one marriage at a time and requires a lawyer for divorce.

volljaehrig.q: At what age does a person come of age in Germany?
volljaehrig.body: In Germany a person is {{volljährig}} at 18. {{Voll}} means full and {{jährig}} means years old: of full age. From this age the law treats a person as an adult. The wrong options are 16, 19 and 21.
volljaehrig.meaning: of age, an adult in law
volljaehrig.front: At what age does a person become an adult in law in Germany?

strafmuendig.q: What happens when a young person of 14 breaks a criminal law?
strafmuendig.body: From the age of 14, a young person is {{strafmündig}}: criminally responsible. {{Strafe}} means punishment, and {{mündig}} means responsible for oneself. A person of 14 or older who breaks a criminal law is punished. The young person is punished, not the parents, and special rules for young people apply. A child under 14 is not punished.
strafmuendig.front: From what age can a young person be punished for a crime?

alter-14-18.title: Two ages in the law
head: From 14
From 18
rows: of age, an adult in law

paar.q: Which couple may not live together in Germany?
paar.body: Age decides which couple is not allowed. German law calls a person under 14 a child, and an adult may not live with a child as a couple. The law protects children. The other couples in the options are all adults, so they may live together, also two men or two women.
paar.case: Anne is 13 and Tim is 25, so they may not live together as a couple.
paar.front: Which couple is not allowed in Germany? Think of the ages.
paar.back: a child and an adult, for example 13 and 25 years
paar.note: A child is a person under 14.

falle-paar.text: A wrong option shows two men or two women, or a big age gap. These couples are allowed because both partners are adults. Only the age of Anne (13) decides.

kinder-schutz.q: What happens if you hit a child in Germany?
kinder-schutz.body: If you hit a child in Germany, you can be punished. This is true for everyone, also for parents. A child has a right to grow up without violence. So it is not only a private matter of the family.
kinder-schutz.front: What happens if someone hits a child in Germany?
kinder-schutz.back: You can be punished for it.
kinder-schutz.note: Children have a right to grow up without violence.

eine-ehe.q: How many spouses may a person have at the same time?
eine-ehe.body: In Germany you may be married to **only** one person at a time. Being married to two people at the same time is not allowed, for men and for women. Marrying again is allowed, after a divorce and also after the death of a spouse. Other ways of living are allowed: new partners after a divorce, two women who live together, a single father with his children.
eine-ehe.front: How many spouses may you have at the same time in Germany?
eine-ehe.back: only one spouse at a time
eine-ehe.note: New marriage after divorce or death is fine.

trennungsjahr.q: What does the year of separation mean?
trennungsjahr.body: Married couples may get divorced ({{sich scheiden lassen}}), but usually they must first observe the {{Trennungsjahr}}. {{Trennung}} means separation and {{Jahr}} means year. For at least one year the spouses ({{Ehegatten}}) live their own lives, apart from each other. After that, the divorce is possible.
trennungsjahr.front: How long must spouses usually live apart before a divorce?
trennungsjahr.back: usually at least one year (year of separation)
trennungsjahr.note: Year of living apart, then divorce is possible.

falle-trennungsjahr.text: Wrong options say that the divorce case lasts a year or that the marriage lasted a year. Another wrong option says that the right to see the children applies for a year. The year is the time the spouses live apart before the divorce.

scheidung.q: What do you need for a divorce in Germany?
scheidung.body: {{Ehe}} means marriage and {{Scheidung}} means divorce. A divorce is decided by a court. For it you need the support of a lawyer ({{Anwältin}} or {{Anwalt}}). The lawyer represents you in court. You do not need the consent of your parents or your children, and no certificate from a doctor.
scheidung.front: Who helps you in a German divorce case?
scheidung.note: No consent of parents or children needed.

items.q: At what age is a person of age, and from what age criminally responsible?
items.a: Of age ({{volljährig}}) at 18. Criminally responsible ({{strafmündig}}) from 14.

items.q: Why may Anne (13) and Tim (25) not live together as a couple?
items.a: Anne is under 14, so she is a child. An adult may not live with a child as a couple.

items.q: How many spouses may a person have at once, and may he or she marry again?
items.a: Only one at a time. Marrying again after a divorce or a death is allowed.

items.q: What must spouses usually do before a divorce, and who do they need?
items.a: They live apart for at least one year ({{Trennungsjahr}}). They need the support of a lawyer.

sozialstaat.title: Social market economy and social insurance
sozialstaat.big: Germany's economy follows supply and demand, but the state ensures social balance, for example with social insurance that employers and employees pay.

marktwirtschaft.q: What is Germany's economic system called?
marktwirtschaft.body: Germany's economic system is the {{soziale Marktwirtschaft}}. Supply and demand ({{Angebot und Nachfrage}}) decide what is made and sold. But the state does not leave it to the market alone: it ensures a social balance ({{sozialer Ausgleich}}). Social insurance is one part of this. In a {{Planwirtschaft}} (planned economy) the state plans everything instead.
marktwirtschaft.front: How does Germany's economy work, in one sentence?
marktwirtschaft.back: Social market economy: supply and demand, but the state ensures social balance
marktwirtschaft.note: Not planned by the state, not only the market.

beschaeftigte.q: Where do most working people work?
beschaeftigte.body: Most people in employment work for a company ({{Firma}}) or an authority ({{Behörde}}). They are employees: {{Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer}}. The employer ({{Arbeitgeber}}) gives work, the employee ({{Arbeitnehmer}}) takes it. Fewer people are self-employed ({{selbstständig}}) with their own company.
beschaeftigte.front: Where do most working people in Germany work?
beschaeftigte.back: for a company or a public authority

sozialversicherung.q: Who pays social insurance, and how?
sozialversicherung.body: Anyone in regular employment ({{fest angestellt}}) pays {{Sozialversicherung}} automatically. The employee's share is taken from the wage, and the employer pays a share too. So employers and employees pay, not **only** one side. The money is called {{Sozialabgaben}} (social contributions). Church tax, donations and club fees do not finance it.
sozialversicherung.front: Who pays social insurance, and with what?
sozialversicherung.back: Employers and employees together, with social contributions

versicherungen.q: Which insurances are part of social insurance?
versicherungen.body: Social insurance has five parts: {{Krankenversicherung}} (health), {{Pflegeversicherung}} (long-term care), {{Rentenversicherung}} (pension), {{Arbeitslosenversicherung}} (unemployment) and {{Unfallversicherung}} (accident). Together they create social security. They help when people fall ill, need care, grow old, lose their job or have an accident. Private insurances such as {{Lebensversicherung}} (life), {{Autoversicherung}} (car) and {{Haftpflichtversicherung}} (liability) are **not** part of it.
versicherungen.front: Name the five parts of social insurance.
versicherungen.back: Health, long-term care, pension, unemployment and accident insurance
versicherungen.note: Life insurance is private, not part of it.

sozial-oder-privat.title: Social insurance or private insurance?
head: Part of social insurance
Not part of it
rows: a private contract that you choose

falle-pflege.text: In the question about {{Pflegeversicherung}}, a wrong option is {{Unfallversicherung}}. It is another branch of social insurance, not a group that contains care insurance. The group is {{Sozialversicherung}}.

gehalt.q: What is not taken from an employee's salary?
gehalt.body: From the salary ({{Gehalt}}), an employee pays wage tax ({{Lohnsteuer}}) and contributions to health, pension and unemployment insurance. The employer takes these amounts automatically. Value added tax ({{Umsatzsteuer}}, also called {{Mehrwertsteuer}}) is **not** paid from the salary. It is already part of the price when you buy something.
gehalt.case: Ms Frost works in an office as a permanent employee. Wage tax and insurance contributions are taken from her salary, value added tax is not.
gehalt.front: Which tax is not paid from an employee's salary?
gehalt.note: It is part of the price of goods.

falle-nicht.text: Two questions ask what does **not** belong. Life insurance is not social insurance, and value added tax is not paid from the salary. Read the word {{nicht}} first.

items.q: What does {{soziale Marktwirtschaft}} mean?
items.a: Supply and demand decide, but the state ensures a social balance.

items.q: Who pays social insurance, and how does the money reach it?
items.a: Employers and employees pay together. The contributions ({{Sozialabgaben}}) are taken automatically from the wage.

items.q: Which common insurance is not part of social insurance?
items.a: The {{Lebensversicherung}}. It is private.

items.q: Why does an employee not pay {{Umsatzsteuer}} from the salary?
items.a: Because {{Umsatzsteuer}} is part of the price of goods. It is not a contribution taken from the pay.

arbeitsrecht.title: Rights at work
arbeitsrecht.big: Employees have rights: unions and the works council speak for them, pregnant women are protected, and the labour court settles disputes.

gewerkschaft.body: Trade unions ({{Gewerkschaften}}) are interest groups ({{Interessenverbände}}) of employees. They represent {{Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer}}. They do **not** represent employers, companies or the self-employed. One employee alone has little power. Together, employees speak with one voice.
gewerkschaft.front: Whom do trade unions speak for?
gewerkschaft.note: Not employers, not companies, not the self-employed.

betriebsrat.q: Who helps employees inside a company?
betriebsrat.body: The {{Betriebsrat}} (works council) helps employees with problems with their employer. {{Betrieb}} is a company or workplace. {{Rat}} is a council. The employees of the company elect it.
betriebsrat.front: Which body inside a company helps employees with problems with the boss?

gewerkschaft-betriebsrat.title: Trade union and works council
head: {{Gewerkschaft}}
{{Betriebsrat}}
rows: a council that the employees of one company elect
common interests of employees, for example pay
help with problems with the employer

falle-betriebs.text: The wrong options also begin with {{Betriebs}}: {{Betriebsprüfer}} (company auditor), {{Betriebsgruppe}} and {{Betriebsmanagement}} (company management). Only the {{Betriebsrat}} is a council of the employees. The management leads the company for the employer.

mutterschutz.q: How does the law protect pregnant women?
mutterschutz.body: A pregnant woman is specially protected by law shortly before and after the birth. This protection is called {{Mutterschutz}}: {{Mutter}} is mother, {{Schutz}} is protection. It protects the health of mother and child and the woman's job. A boss must **not** dismiss a woman because she is expecting a child and the boss knows it.
mutterschutz.front: What is the legal protection of mothers around the birth called?
mutterschutz.note: A boss must not dismiss her because she is pregnant.

falle-eltern.text: The wrong options sound close, but none is the name of this protection. {{Elternzeit}} is parental leave, {{Wochenbett}} is the time after the birth, {{Geburtsvorbereitung}} is preparation for the birth. The protection is called {{Mutterschutz}}.

kuendigungsfrist.q: What must you observe when you end your job?
kuendigungsfrist.body: Ending a job is called {{Kündigung}}: it can come from the employee or from the employer. If you end your job yourself, you must observe the notice period ({{Kündigungsfrist}}). {{Frist}} is a time limit. The notice period is the time between your notice and your last day at work. Its length is set by law or by your contract.
kuendigungsfrist.front: What time limit must you observe when you end your job?

arbeitsgericht.q: Which court decides conflicts at work?
arbeitsgericht.body: The {{Arbeitsgericht}} (labour court) is responsible for conflicts in the world of work. {{Arbeit}} is work, {{Gericht}} is court. A typical case is an unjustified dismissal by the boss. A wrong utility bill, problems with neighbours or a traffic accident are not about work. Other courts, such as the {{Familiengericht}}, the {{Strafgericht}} and the {{Amtsgericht}}, deal with other matters.
arbeitsgericht.front: Which court is responsible for conflicts between employee and employer?

kuendigungsschutzklage.q: What can you do after an unlawful dismissal?
kuendigungsschutzklage.body: If your employer dismisses you unlawfully ({{zu Unrecht}}), you can file a {{Kündigungsschutzklage}} at the labour court. The parts: {{Kündigung}} is dismissal, {{Schutz}} is protection, {{Klage}} is a lawsuit. Working on and being friendly to the boss does not challenge the dismissal. A {{Mahnverfahren}} (dunning procedure) is for unpaid money, not for a dismissal. The police do not handle a wrong dismissal.
kuendigungsschutzklage.case: Your boss dismisses you without a justified reason. You file the action at the labour court.
kuendigungsschutzklage.front: What do you file against an unlawful dismissal?
kuendigungsschutzklage.back: file a Kündigungsschutzklage (action for protection against dismissal)
kuendigungsschutzklage.note: Kündigung, Schutz, Klage: dismissal, protection, lawsuit.

items.q: What is the difference between a {{Gewerkschaft}} and a {{Betriebsrat}}?
items.a: A {{Gewerkschaft}} acts across many companies. A {{Betriebsrat}} acts inside one company. Both stand up for employees.

items.q: Why must a boss not dismiss a woman because she is pregnant?
items.a: Because the law protects pregnant women specially, shortly before and after the birth: {{Mutterschutz}}.

items.q: Where do you go after an unlawful dismissal, and what do you file?
items.a: You go to the {{Arbeitsgericht}}. You file a {{Kündigungsschutzklage}}.

items.q: What must you observe when you end your job yourself?
items.a: The notice period: {{Kündigungsfrist}}.

alltag-behoerden.title: Authorities, training and complaints
alltag-behoerden.big: For a licence, an apprenticeship, a wrong tax assessment or a broken product, you need to know where to go.

gaststaette.q: What does a couple need to open a restaurant?
gaststaette.body: To open a restaurant, a couple needs a {{Gaststättenerlaubnis}} (restaurant licence). {{Gaststätte}} is a restaurant or pub, {{Erlaubnis}} is a permit. It comes from the competent authority ({{zuständige Behörde}}). A party is not an authority. The police and the {{Einwohnermeldeamt}} (residents' registration office) do not give this licence.
gaststaette.front: What licence does a couple need to open a restaurant?
gaststaette.back: a restaurant licence from the competent authority
gaststaette.note: Not from the police, a party or the registration office.

biz.q: What does the BIZ help with?
biz.body: The {{Berufsinformationszentrum}} ({{BIZ}}) belongs to the Federal Employment Agency ({{Bundesagentur für Arbeit}}). It helps with the search for an apprenticeship ({{Lehrstellensuche}}). {{Beruf}} is a profession, so the BIZ gives information about jobs. Pensions, tax returns and health insurance are not its tasks.
biz.front: Which centre of the Federal Employment Agency helps you find an apprenticeship?
biz.note: Beruf: profession. It helps with Lehrstellensuche.

weiterlernen.q: What should adults do when work changes fast?
weiterlernen.body: What you must be able to do for work changes very quickly. So adults must keep learning, even after their training ({{Ausbildung}}). School alone is **not** enough for a whole working life. The answer is to learn, not to stop working earlier.
weiterlernen.front: What must adults do, because the skills for work change fast?
weiterlernen.back: Adults must keep learning even after their training.
weiterlernen.note: Work changes fast, so learning does not end.

einspruch.q: What do you do about a wrong tax assessment?
einspruch.body: A tax assessment ({{Steuerbescheid}}) is the letter from the tax office ({{Finanzamt}}) that sets your tax. If it is wrong, you must lodge an objection: {{Einspruch einlegen}}. If you do nothing, the assessment stays valid. Throwing it away or waiting for another letter does not change it.
einspruch.front: What must you do against a wrong tax assessment?
einspruch.note: Doing nothing leaves the assessment valid.

reklamation.q: What can you do if a bought product is broken?
reklamation.body: If a product you bought is broken, you make a complaint: {{reklamieren}}. You tell the shop where you bought it. A broken television is a matter between you and the shop. An {{Anzeige}} is a report to the police, so it is the wrong step. Exchanging the device yourself without asking is wrong too.
reklamation.meaning: to make a complaint about a faulty product
reklamation.case: You unpack a new television at home and it does not work. You take your complaint to the shop.
reklamation.front: What do you do when a product you bought is broken?
reklamation.note: Not Anzeige: that is a report to the police.

drei-wege.title: Three ways to object
head: {{Einspruch}}
{{Kündigungsschutzklage}}
{{Reklamation}}
rows: do nothing or throw the letter away

items.q: What do you need to open a restaurant, and who gives it?
items.a: A {{Gaststättenerlaubnis}} from the competent authority ({{zuständige Behörde}}).

items.q: Which centre of the Federal Employment Agency helps with the search for an apprenticeship?
items.a: The {{Berufsinformationszentrum}} ({{BIZ}}).

items.q: Why must adults keep learning after their training?
items.a: Because what you must be able to do for work changes very quickly.

items.q: What do you do about a wrong tax assessment, and what about a broken television?
items.a: {{Einspruch einlegen}} at the tax office. {{Reklamieren}} at the shop.

kinder-eltern.title: Parents and children
kinder-eltern.big: Parents bring up their children, the {{Jugendamt}} helps and protects, and adult children decide about their own lives.

erziehung.q: Whose task is it to bring up children?
erziehung.body: Bringing up children is above all the task of the parents ({{Eltern}}). The Basic Law ({{Grundgesetz}}) gives parents this right and names it their first duty. The state, the schools and relatives may help, but they do not come first.
erziehung.front: Who has the first duty to bring up a child?
erziehung.note: The Basic Law names it their first duty.

kindergarten.q: Who decides about kindergarten, and who has a claim to a place?
kindergarten.body: The parents decide whether a child goes to {{Kindergarten}}. It is their choice, not a duty. From the age of 3 until school starts, a child has a legal claim ({{Anspruch}}) to a place, a {{Kindergartenplatz}}. The state, the federal states and the schools do not decide.
kindergarten.meaning: the place for young children before school
kindergarten.front: Who decides about kindergarten, and what can a child claim from age 3?
kindergarten.back: the parents; a place in kindergarten

elterngeld.q: How does a parent get parental allowance?
elterngeld.body: {{Elterngeld}} is parental allowance: money for parents after the birth of a child. It does not come automatically. The parent must submit an application ({{Antrag}}) at the {{Elterngeldstelle}}. The health insurance fund and the employment office are not the place to apply.
elterngeld.case: Ms Seger is going to have a child. To get {{Elterngeld}}, she submits an application at the {{Elterngeldstelle}}.
elterngeld.front: Where must a parent apply for parental allowance?
elterngeld.back: submit an application at the parental allowance office

jugendamt.q: Which office helps with problems in bringing up children?
jugendamt.body: Parents who have problems bringing up their children can get help from the {{Jugendamt}}. {{Jugend}} means youth and {{Amt}} means office. The {{Jugendamt}} may also take a child out of the family. This is allowed when the child is beaten or has to go hungry. The state watches over how children are brought up, so it can protect a child in danger.
jugendamt.front: Which office helps with upbringing problems and can take a child from the family?

falle-aemter.text: The wrong options are other offices: {{Ordnungsamt}} (public order), {{Schulamt}} (schools), {{Gesundheitsamt}} (health) and {{Einwohnermeldeamt}} (registration of residents). Each has its own task, and a doctor is not the place for this either.

falle-jugendamt.text: A wrong option gives the {{Jugendamt}} another job. It does not decide which school a child attends, does not pay child benefit ({{Kindergeld}}) and does not check kindergarten attendance.

volljaehrig.q: What may parents do when an adult daughter makes her own choice?
volljaehrig.body: In Germany a person is {{volljährig}} (of age) at 18. An adult decides about their own life, for example where and with whom to live. Parents must respect these decisions. They have no right to bring an adult child home or to choose a partner.
volljaehrig.case: A 22-year-old woman lives with her boyfriend, and her parents do not like him. They must respect her decision and cannot report her to the police for this.
volljaehrig.front: What must parents do when an adult daughter chooses how she lives?
volljaehrig.back: respect the decision of their adult daughter

items.q: Who has the first duty to bring up a child, and who may step in if a child is in danger?
items.a: The parents. The {{Jugendamt}} may take a child out of the family if the child is beaten or has to go hungry.

items.q: What must a parent do to get {{Elterngeld}}?
items.a: Submit an application at the {{Elterngeldstelle}}. It is not paid automatically.

items.q: From what age until school does a child have a claim to a place in kindergarten?
items.a: From the age of 3. The parents decide whether the child goes.

items.q: At what age is a person {{volljährig}}, and what follows for the parents?
items.a: At 18. Parents must respect the decisions of an adult child.

schule.title: School and learning
schule.big: School is compulsory, the state supervises it, and adults can catch up on school qualifications and keep learning.

schulpflicht.q: Which duty do most children in Germany have?
schulpflicht.body: Most children in Germany must go to school. This is the {{Schulpflicht}}: {{Schule}} means school and {{Pflicht}} means duty. At school, a child has a duty to be present, the {{Anwesenheitspflicht}}. {{Anwesenheit}} means presence.
schulpflicht.front: What is the duty to go to school called, and the duty to be present in class?

falle-pflicht.text: The wrong options also end in {{Pflicht}}: {{Wahlpflicht}} (compulsory voting), {{Schweigepflicht}} (duty of confidentiality), {{Religionspflicht}} (compulsory religion). For most children **only** the {{Schulpflicht}} applies. In class, the duty is to attend, not unlimited free time or free choice of all subjects.

schulaufsicht.q: Why does the state supervise schools?
schulaufsicht.body: The state supervises the whole school system ({{Schulwesen}}). The reason is the Basic Law ({{Grundgesetz}}): it makes this a task of the state. Other reasons sound sensible, but only the Basic Law is the reason.
schulaufsicht.front: On what basis does the state supervise schools?
schulaufsicht.back: Because under the Basic Law it is its task.

abitur.q: Which qualification leads to university, and where can adults catch it up?
abitur.body: Normally one needs the {{Abitur}} to start a degree at a university ({{Universität}}). Adults who do not have it can catch it up ({{nachholen}}) at an {{Abendgymnasium}} (evening grammar school). {{Abend}} means evening: the classes take place in the evening.
abitur.meaning: the qualification needed to start university
abitur.case: A man of 30 wants to catch up on his {{Abitur}}. He can do this at an {{Abendgymnasium}}.
abitur.front: Which qualification do you normally need to start university, and where can adults catch it up?
abitur.back: the Abitur; at an evening grammar school

falle-hochschule.text: A {{Diplom}} is a degree after studying, and a {{Gesellenprüfung}} ends a trade apprenticeship. Neither opens the way to university. To catch up on the Abitur, a {{Hochschule}}, a {{Privatuniversität}} and a {{Hauptschule}} are wrong.

weiterbildung.q: What is the adult education centre for?
weiterbildung.body: The {{Volkshochschule}} is an institution for further education ({{Weiterbildung}}). {{Weiter}} means further and {{Bildung}} means education. It is not **only** for young people and not **only** for pensioners. It is also not a place for religious education.
weiterbildung.front: What kind of institution is the adult education centre?

ausbildung.q: What gives the best chances of a well-paid job?
ausbildung.body: Good training gives the best chances of a well-paid job ({{Arbeitsplatz}}). A person with good training is {{gut ausgebildet}} (well trained). The best chances do not come from religion, gender or party membership.
ausbildung.front: What gives the best chances of a well-paid job in Germany?
ausbildung.note: Not religion, not gender, not party membership.

fuehrerschein.q: Can someone get a driving licence if German is not their mother tongue?
fuehrerschein.body: Having another mother tongue ({{Muttersprache}}) is no reason to be refused a {{Führerschein}}. A person may be able to take the theory test ({{Theorieprüfung}}) in their mother tongue. More than 10 languages are on offer. A person does not first have to live in Germany for ten years. Nobody has to go to another country for the test.
fuehrerschein.case: A young woman is afraid of the driving test because German is not her mother tongue.
fuehrerschein.front: A woman's mother tongue is not German. What may she do for the driving theory test?
fuehrerschein.back: possibly take the theory test in her mother tongue
fuehrerschein.note: More than 10 languages to choose from.

items.q: What do the two parts of {{Schulpflicht}} mean?
items.a: {{Schule}} is school, {{Pflicht}} is duty: most children must go to school.

items.q: Why does the state supervise the school system?
items.a: Because the {{Grundgesetz}} makes it a task of the state.

items.q: Where can an adult catch up on the {{Abitur}}, and why is a {{Hochschule}} wrong?
items.a: At an {{Abendgymnasium}}. A {{Hochschule}} is a place to study after the {{Abitur}}.

items.q: What is the {{Volkshochschule}} for, and what gives the best chances of a well-paid job?
items.a: Further education ({{Weiterbildung}}). Good training gives the best chances.

zusammenleben.title: Living together
zusammenleben.big: Neighbours follow shared rules, many people work without pay in clubs, and special achievements are honoured.

nachtruhe.q: From what time must people keep quiet at night?
nachtruhe.body: The statutory quiet hours at night ({{Nachtruhe}}) begin at 22 Uhr, which is 10 p.m. {{Nacht}} means night and {{Ruhe}} means quiet. The law sets the time: it does not depend on the sun or on when the neighbours go to sleep. It is also not midnight ({{0 Uhr}}).
nachtruhe.front: At what time do the statutory quiet hours begin?

hausordnung.q: What is in the house rules of an apartment building?
hausordnung.body: Most apartment buildings ({{Mietshäuser}}) in Germany have a {{Hausordnung}}. {{Haus}} means house and {{Ordnung}} means order or rules. It names rules that all residents must follow. It is also not about public transport and does not give the address of the {{Ordnungsamt}} (public order office).
hausordnung.front: What do the house rules of a building state?
hausordnung.back: rules that all residents must follow

ehrenamt.q: What does voluntary work mean in Germany?
ehrenamt.body: People who work {{ehrenamtlich}} do voluntary work in their free time. They work voluntarily and **unpaid**, for example in clubs ({{Vereine}}) and associations ({{Verbände}}). {{Ehre}} means honour and {{Amt}} means office. A job for pay is not an {{Ehrenamt}}, even in a hospital.
ehrenamt.front: What do people do who have an Ehrenamt?
ehrenamt.back: work voluntarily and unpaid in clubs and associations
ehrenamt.note: Ehre: honour. Amt: office. No pay.

verdienstkreuz.q: What honours outstanding achievements in the Federal Republic?
verdienstkreuz.body: The {{Bundesverdienstkreuz}} honours outstanding achievements in the political, economic, cultural, intellectual or social field. {{Bund}} means federation, {{Verdienst}} means merit here and {{Kreuz}} means cross. It is an honour of the Federal Republic.
verdienstkreuz.front: Which honour does the Federal Republic give for outstanding achievements?
verdienstkreuz.note: Bund: federation. Verdienst: merit. Kreuz: cross.

falle-ehrung.text: Two wrong options are honours of the former GDR: the {{Vaterländischer Verdienstorden}} and the title {{Held der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik}}. The {{Bundesadler}} is the Federal Eagle, a symbol of the state, not an honour.

items.q: At what time do the statutory quiet hours begin?
items.a: At 22 Uhr (10 p.m.), not at midnight.

items.q: Who must follow the {{Hausordnung}} of a building?
items.a: All residents of the building.

items.q: What does {{ehrenamtlich}} mean?
items.a: Voluntary and unpaid, for example in clubs and associations.

items.q: What is the {{Bundesverdienstkreuz}} given for?
items.a: For outstanding achievements in the political, economic, cultural, intellectual or social field.

religion-feste.title: Religion, church tax and festivals
religion-feste.big: Everyone in Germany may believe what they want, and Christianity still shapes the festivals and customs of the year.

toleranz.body: Religious tolerance ({{religiöse Toleranz}}) means that everyone can believe what they want. Some people believe in no god, and that is allowed too. The state does not decide which god people believe in. Every religion may have its own house of prayer, for example a church, a mosque or a synagogue.
toleranz.front: In Germany, who decides what a person believes?
toleranz.back: Everyone can believe what they want.

christentum.q: Which religion shaped culture in Germany and Europe?
christentum.body: Christianity ({{Christentum}}) has shaped European and German culture for many centuries. Many holidays come from it, for example {{Weihnachten}} (Christmas) and {{Ostern}} (Easter). The wrong options are {{der Hinduismus}}, {{der Buddhismus}} and {{der Islam}}. People practise these religions in Germany too, and they are free to do so.
christentum.front: Which religion shaped culture in Germany and Europe?

kirchensteuer.q: Why does the tax return ask about church membership?
kirchensteuer.body: People who belong to a church pay a church tax ({{Kirchensteuer}}). It is tied to income tax ({{Einkommensteuer}}) and wage tax ({{Lohnsteuer}}). So the tax return ({{Steuererklärung}}) asks whether you belong to a church. People without a church do not pay this tax.
kirchensteuer.front: What tax is the reason for the church question in the tax return?
kirchensteuer.back: There is a church tax. It is tied to income tax and wage tax.

falle-kirchensteuer.text: A wrong option says people without a church pay more tax. That is wrong: they pay **no** church tax. Statistics and the church are not the reason either.

weihnachten.q: What is the time before Christmas, and what is a Christmas custom?
weihnachten.body: The last four weeks before Christmas ({{Weihnachten}}) are the {{Adventszeit}}. {{Zeit}} means time or period. The wrong options are single days in autumn.
