They are {{Buß- und Bettag}} (Day of Repentance and Prayer), {{Erntedankfest}} (harvest festival) and {{Allerheiligen}} (All Saints' Day). A custom ({{Brauch}}) at Christmas is to decorate a fir tree ({{Tannenbaum}}).
weihnachten.meaning: Advent, the four weeks before Christmas
weihnachten.front: What are the four weeks before Christmas called, and what is one Christmas custom?
weihnachten.back: Advent, the four weeks before Christmas; decorating a fir tree
weihnachten.note: Zeit means a period of time.

ostern.q: What is a custom at Easter?
ostern.body: At Easter ({{Ostern}}) people in Germany paint eggs ({{Eier bemalen}}). Many families also hide the eggs for children. Easter is a Christian holiday in spring.
ostern.front: What do people do with eggs at Easter?
ostern.note: Eggs belong to Easter, the fir tree to Christmas.

falle-braeuche.text: The wrong options are customs of other days. Eggs belong to Easter, the fir tree to Christmas, costumes and masks to {{Rosenmontag}}. Pumpkins and rockets belong to other days of the year.

pfingsten.q: What kind of holiday is Pentecost?
pfingsten.body: Pentecost ({{Pfingsten}}) is a Christian holiday ({{christlicher Feiertag}}). It falls 7 weeks after Easter. People celebrate it in all of Germany, not only in Bavaria. It is **not** a day of remembrance ({{Gedenktag}}) or a day of mourning ({{Trauertag}}).
pfingsten.front: What kind of holiday is Pentecost?
pfingsten.note: Easter and Christmas are Christian too.

rosenmontag.q: At which festival do people wear costumes and masks?
rosenmontag.body: On {{Rosenmontag}} (Rose Monday) many people in Germany wear colourful costumes and masks. It is a Monday in the carnival season, in February or March. The wrong options are different events: {{Maifeiertag}} (May Day, 1 May), {{Oktoberfest}} and {{Pfingsten}}.
rosenmontag.front: On which day do people dress up in masks and costumes?

feste-im-jahr.title: Festivals of the year
head: When
Custom or meaning
rows: A period of time, not one day

items.q: What does religious tolerance mean in Germany?
items.a: Everyone can believe what they want. The state does not decide which god people believe in.

items.q: Why does the tax return ask whether you belong to a church?
items.a: Because there is a church tax. It is tied to income tax and wage tax.

items.q: Which custom belongs to {{Weihnachten}}, {{Ostern}} and {{Rosenmontag}}?
items.a: {{Weihnachten}}: decorate a fir tree. {{Ostern}}: paint eggs. {{Rosenmontag}}: wear costumes and masks.

items.q: What are the four weeks before Christmas called, and what kind of holiday is {{Pfingsten}}?
items.a: The {{Adventszeit}}. {{Pfingsten}} is a Christian holiday.

juedisches-leben-migration.title: Jewish life and migration
juedisches-leben-migration.big: Jewish life in Germany is about 1700 years old, and migrants from many countries came to the Federal Republic and the GDR.

juedische-gemeinde.q: How long has there been Jewish life in Germany?
juedische-gemeinde.body: The first Jewish community ({{jüdische Gemeinde}}) in the area of today's Germany existed about 1700 years ago. The wrong options say about 300, 700 or 1150 years. All three are too short.
juedische-gemeinde.front: How long ago was the first Jewish community in Germany?

berlin-muenchen.q: Which cities have the largest Jewish communities?
berlin-muenchen.body: The two largest Jewish communities in Germany are in Berlin and Munich (München). Worms and Speyer have a very old Jewish history, but their communities are small today. The communities in Hamburg, Essen, Nuremberg and Stuttgart are smaller too.
berlin-muenchen.front: Which two cities have the largest Jewish communities in Germany?
berlin-muenchen.note: Worms and Speyer are old, but small today.

synagoge.q: What is the Jewish house of prayer called?
synagoge.body: The Jewish house of prayer ({{Gebetshaus}}) is the synagogue ({{Synagoge}}). {{Gebet}} means prayer and {{Haus}} means house. The wrong options are houses of prayer of other religions. {{Kirche}} (church) and {{Basilika}} (basilica, a type of church) are Christian. {{Moschee}} (mosque) is Muslim.
synagoge.meaning: synagogue, the Jewish house of prayer
synagoge.front: What is the Jewish place of prayer called?
synagoge.note: Kirche is Christian, Moschee is Muslim.

makkabi.q: Who may join a Maccabi sports club?
makkabi.body: {{Makkabi}} is the name of Jewish sports clubs in Germany. There are roughly 40 of them. They are Jewish clubs, but all people may become members. Membership is not **only** for Germans, Israelis or religious people.
makkabi.front: Who may join a Jewish Maccabi sports club?

gastarbeiter.q: Who were the guest workers, and where did the first come from?
gastarbeiter.body: In the 1950s and 1960s the Federal Republic recruited workers from other countries. Its economy was growing fast and needed more workers. These workers were called guest workers: {{Gastarbeiter}} (men) and {{Gastarbeiterinnen}} (women). {{Gast}} means guest and {{Arbeiter}} means worker. The first guest workers came from Italy ({{Italien}}).
gastarbeiter.front: What were workers recruited from abroad called, and from which country did the first come?
gastarbeiter.back: Guest workers; the first came from Italy

falle-arbeiter.text: {{Schwarzarbeiter}} (undeclared workers), {{Zeitarbeiter}} (temporary agency workers) and {{Schichtarbeiter}} (shift workers) also end in {{Arbeiter}}. They name kinds of work, not workers recruited from abroad. Only {{Gastarbeiter}} is right.

tuerkei.q: Which country do most migrants come from?
tuerkei.body: Migrants ({{Migrantinnen und Migranten}}) are people who came to Germany from another country to live here. More of them came from Turkey ({{Türkei}}) than from any other country. Many families from Turkey came because the Federal Republic also recruited guest workers there. Italy ({{Italien}}), Poland ({{Polen}}) and Morocco ({{Marokko}}) are also countries of origin, but Turkey is the largest.
tuerkei.meaning: migrants, people who moved here from abroad
tuerkei.front: Which country has sent the most migrants to Germany?
tuerkei.note: Italy: first guest workers. Turkey: most migrants.

falle-italien-tuerkei.text: {{Türkei}} and {{Italien}} are easy to mix up. Most migrants came from Turkey. But the **first** guest workers came from Italy.

ddr-migranten.q: Where did migrants in the GDR come from?
ddr-migranten.body: In the GDR ({{DDR}}), the East German state, migrants came mainly from Vietnam, Poland ({{Polen}}) and Mozambique ({{Mosambik}}). Many of them came to work in GDR companies. Each wrong option lists three other countries, so remember the three together.
ddr-migranten.meaning: the German Democratic Republic, East Germany
ddr-migranten.front: From which three countries did migrants in the GDR mainly come?

items.q: How old is Jewish life in Germany, and in which two cities are the largest communities?
items.a: About 1700 years. The largest communities are in Berlin and Munich.

items.q: What is the Jewish house of prayer, and who may join a Maccabi club?
items.a: The {{Synagoge}}. All people may join.

items.q: Why did the Federal Republic recruit guest workers, and where did the first come from?
items.a: Its economy grew fast and needed workers. The first came from Italy, not from Turkey.

items.q: Which country do most migrants come from, and which countries did migrants in the GDR come from?
items.a: Most migrants come from Turkey. In the GDR they came from Vietnam, Poland and Mozambique.
